title: Coarse moduli schemes restrict to open substacks
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over $k$ with finite diagonal and a coarse moduli scheme $q:\mathcal X\to Q$, with stack, coarse moduli, algebraic space and 2-fibre product as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Finite diagonal means that every scheme base change of the diagonal is a finite scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $\mathcal U\subset\mathcal X$ be an open substack: for every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, its 2-base change is an open subscheme of $T$. Then there is a unique open subscheme $V\subset Q$ with $\mathcal U\simeq\mathcal X\times_Q V$, and the restriction $q|_{\mathcal U}:\mathcal U\to V$ is a coarse moduli morphism, initial among maps to algebraic spaces and bijective on geometric isomorphism classes. Schemes and finite type are [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori), universal-homeomorphism and uniform categorical properties; Tag 0DUV (lemma-etale-separated-over-keel-mori), applied to an open immersion. Open-substack formulation is the agent-written consequence, not a verbatim lemma.

proof.text: Apply the finite-diagonal Keel--Mori node to $\mathcal X/k$. Its hypotheses are the given Deligne--Mumford property and finite relative diagonal; no smoothness or tameness is required. Obtain $c:\mathcal X\to M$, uniform categorical and a universal homeomorphism, where $M$ is an algebraic space. In particular $|c|$ is a homeomorphism. This invocation is independent of the given coarse scheme $Q$ and of the open $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori) and Tag 0DUG (definition-categorical-quotient); open-restriction consequence with stacks-properties.tex Tag 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks).

proof.text: Use the categorical part of the definition of the given coarse map $q$ and the categorical part of $c$. They supply unique maps $a:Q\to M$ and $b:M\to Q$ over $k$ with $aq=c$ and $bc=q$. Hence $(ba)q=q$ and $(ab)c=c$; uniqueness of factorization for $q$ and $c$ gives $ba=\mathrm{id}_Q$ and $ab=\mathrm{id}_M$. Thus $a$ identifies $Q$ with $M$ and identifies $q$ with $c$. In particular $|q|$ is a homeomorphism. It also identifies every flat base change of $q$ with the corresponding flat base change of $c$, so $q$ is uniform categorical. This uses only uniqueness of the two universal properties, not scheme representability of $M$ in advance.

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori) and Tag 0DUG (definition-categorical-quotient); open-restriction consequence with stacks-properties.tex Tag 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks).

proof.text: By the stack-topology node $W=|\mathcal U|$ is open in $|\mathcal X|$. Define $V$ to be the open subscheme of $Q$ with underlying subset $|q|(W)$, using the open-subscheme convention. The homeomorphism from step 2 gives $|q|^{-1}(|V|)=W$. The 2-base change $\mathcal X\times_Q V$ is an open substack: after any scheme $T\to\mathcal X$ it is the inverse-image open subscheme $T\times_Q V$ of $T$. The inverse-image assertion of the stack-topology node says its point subset is $|q|^{-1}(|V|)$, hence it is the same open substack as $\mathcal U$ by injectivity of that node's classification. This identifies the inclusion of $\mathcal U$ with the displayed 2-base change, over $\mathcal X$. If an open $V'\subseteq Q$ has the same pullback, that classification gives $|q|^{-1}(|V'|)=W$; applying the bijection $|q|$ gives $|V'|=|V|$, hence $V'=V$.

source.place: Tag 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks) and the inverse-image compatibility of open substacks; construction of the inverse-image open on scheme charts.

proof.text: The open inclusion $V\hookrightarrow Q$ is flat: its map on each local ring is an isomorphism, so tensoring over that map is, after identifying the rings, the identity functor and preserves exact sequences. This verifies flatness directly from the definitions of open immersion and flat morphism. Apply the uniform categorical property of $q$ established in step 2 to this flat base change. It says that for every algebraic space $Z/k$, each map $\mathcal X\times_Q V\to Z$ factors uniquely through $V$. Under the equivalence of step 3 the projection is exactly $q|_{\mathcal U}$. It is therefore initial among maps from $\mathcal U$ to algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 0DUT (theorem-keel-mori) and Tag 0DUG (definition-categorical-quotient); open-restriction consequence with stacks-properties.tex Tag 06FJ (lemma-open-substacks).

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed field extension $\Omega/k$. By the 2-fibre-product definition and step 3, objects of $\mathcal U(\Omega)$ are exactly the objects $x\in\mathcal X(\Omega)$ for which $q(x)\in Q(\Omega)$ factors through $V$, with the same isomorphisms between them. Indeed an open inclusion is a monomorphism, so the lift to $V$ is unique when it exists. The coarse property of $q$ is a bijection between isomorphism classes of $\mathcal X(\Omega)$ and $Q(\Omega)$. Restricting this bijection to the indicated subsets gives the required bijection between isomorphism classes of $\mathcal U(\Omega)$ and $V(\Omega)$. Together with step 4 and uniqueness of $V$ from step 3 this proves every assertion, including the empty-open case.
